comments.note: The if (candidates.length === 0) return; early exit was removed from propagateDependencyReblock to allow the COMPLETE-dependent warning and synthesis_generated reset to run even when there are no re-blocked candidates. The function now always runs to the root index write. This is a minor inefficiency for the zero-candidates path (one extra store.readRootIndex + writeRootIndex with no mutations) but ensures correctness without conditional paths.

The COMPLETE dependent warning adds comments to the LAST pipeline. If a WP has no pipelines at all (empty array), the warning is silently skipped. This edge case is unlikely in practice (COMPLETE WPs must have passed their documentation pipeline) but could be documented as a known limitation.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (propagateDependencyReblock): When candidates.length === 0 (no re-blocking occurs), the function still reads and writes the root index (to update last_updated and pending_work_packages). This is a minor no-op write on the zero-candidate path. Low impact but a micro-optimization would be to skip the root write when rootIndex was not mutated.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (propagateDependencyReblock): The COMPLETE-dependent warning appends to the last pipeline's comments. If lastPipeline is null (empty pipelines array), the warning is silently dropped. This is a known edge case documented in the implementation pipeline. Since COMPLETE WPs must have passed a documentation pipeline, this scenario is unreachable in normal workflow order.

summary: Reviewed propagateDependencyReblock three-phase structure: re-block candidates, warn COMPLETE dependents, reset synthesis_generated.
No blocking issues found. All five acceptance criteria verified through code reading and test review.
Filter logic is correct: COMPLETE WPs are excluded from candidates and handled separately, preventing double-processing.
Candidates/COMPLETE-dependent separation is architecturally clean and avoids the risk of modifying a WP via two paths in the same lock.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (propagateDependencyReblock, line 933): The activePipelines loop correctly iterates all IN_PROGRESS pipelines and sets status=FAIL, auto_cancelled=true, completed_at, and summary. Note that p.summary is replaced entirely (= [...]) rather than appended. Any partial progress notes recorded via ledger_update_pipeline_progress on the pipeline are lost. This is the correct behavior for an auto-cancel (the work is void) but worth documenting as an intentional lossy operation in the function's JSDoc.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (propagateDependencyReblock, phase 2, line 961): The COMPLETE-dependent warning loop calls store.writeWorkPackage for each COMPLETE dependent individually, inside the same lock. This is correct and safe. However, if there are N COMPLETE dependents and M non-terminal dependents, the function performs N+M individual WP writes inside a single lock. At scale (large projects with many dependents), this could potentially slow down the lock hold time. Not a concern today but worth noting for future batched-write optimization.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (propagateDependencyReblock, ~line 964): lastPipeline null-guard ('if (lastPipeline)') silently drops the warning when a COMPLETE WP has no pipelines. Both Developer and QA documented this. The silent skip is acceptable given COMPLETE WPs must have passed a documentation pipeline in normal workflow order, but a logged warning (or at minimum a JSDoc note) would improve debuggability for out-of-order states.
